prompt:
Extract the single contact record from the user’s note. Use only its label–value lines, which may be reordered and separated by a colon, equals sign, or tab. Ignore surrounding notes and signatures. Return one bare JSON object with exactly the keys name, phone, email, company, country, each with a string or null value. No other text.

Trim each value and collapse whitespace runs to one space. Absent lines, empty values, and the case-insensitive placeholders -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD represent missing values. Return null for missing fields except for the international-phone country fallback below. Never fill a field from notes, signatures, email domains, or company suffixes.

Reserve the country line for country. For the other lines, assign by content: a value containing @ is email; a value that, after removing a leading tel: and an extension, has at least seven digits and consists only of digits, spaces, and + - ( ) . / is phone. If the name-label value ends in a listed legal suffix and the company-label value does not, swap those values before normalising them.

Name: split Last, First at the first comma and reorder to First Last. Remove leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, or Prof, with or without a dot, ignoring case. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics; never transliterate.
Company: remove a trailing legal suffix and its optional preceding comma, ignoring case: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word.
Email: remove surrounding angle brackets and a mailto: prefix, then lowercase the entire address.
Country: convert the explicit country value to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Recognise English, Swedish, and German names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes, and common aliases regardless of case: UK or Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA or U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ.
Phone: drop a leading tel: and an extension such as ext. 12, ext 12, x12, #12, or extension 12. A number is international if it starts with + or 00 after ignoring a leading opening parenthesis. Replace international 00 with +, remove any (0), and strip spaces, dashes, dots, slashes, and parentheses. Keep the written calling code even if it disagrees with the country line. Only if country is missing, fill it from the international calling code when that code identifies one country; shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. For a national phone, strip formatting, remove one leading trunk 0, and prepend + and the normalised record country’s calling code. Without a country, a national phone is null. Output phone strings in E.164: + followed only by digits.
